advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the 10s ceiling in test_repo_isolation_guard.py leaves enough headroom over 5s watchdog + nested-pytest startup on loaded CI, or widen it toward the 12s outer timeout.
evidence: tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:99: `started = time.monotonic()` (started before subprocess.run, so elapsed includes nested pytest startup + import)
tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:102: `assert elapsed < 10, f"watchdog did not bound the blocked probe: {elapsed:.2f}s"`
tests/_isolation.py:26: `GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5` — only ~5s of the ceiling is the watchdog; the remainder is nested-pytest overhead
The hang-guard marker on line 101 sanctions the lint, but sanctioning does not remove the runtime flake risk under contention.
advisory.finding: The `assert elapsed < 10` ceiling bounds the whole nested-pytest run (Python startup + heavy conftest import + collection) plus the 5s inner watchdog, giving only ~2x headroom over the 5s expected wall time. On a heavily loaded CI runner, cold-start + import of the real conftest (which imports rebar modules) can consume several seconds, so total elapsed could exceed 10s while still under the 12s outer timeout, producing a spurious failure — the exact flake class the wall-clock lint warns about.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the shim-count oracle tolerant of >=2 matching probes (assert count >= 2) or document the exact-count coupling to the conftest guard.
evidence: tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:100: `assert state.read_text() == "2", "the shim did not block the second real guard probe"`

tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:50: `if args[-2:] == tail:` — only tail-matched invocations increment the counter, so the exact-2 invariant depends on conftest emitting exactly one probe pair for the operation
tests/conftest.py:603-608: `_no_repo_commits` calls `_repo_head` twice (before/after); tests/conftest.py:688,694: sessionstart/finish call `_repo_porcelain`
advisory.finding: The `assert state.read_text() == "2"` oracle is tightly coupled to the exact number of guard probes emitted in the nested session (one before/after pair for the targeted operation). It relies on no other code path in the real conftest invoking `git rev-parse HEAD` or `git status --porcelain`. If a future conftest change adds another such probe (e.g. an extra isolation check), the count drifts to 3+ and this assertion fails in a way unrelated to the watchdog under test, misattributing the failure.
